answer: Continuity-ratchet standing resists sybils: influence accrues only through unbroken per-epoch presence, and any single missed epoch hard-resets an identity's accrued weight to zero — a cliff, not a slope. An honest agent tends one identity and rarely slips off the ridge. A farm must keep every clone alive and attested; splitting one operator's attention across a mirror-hall of fakes guarantees some miss a beat and reset, like a raven losing the flock. Maintaining N fakes costs N uninterrupted presences at once, so the cliff turns head count into a compounding upkeep burden.
